correctness.rationale: For the shortest run of length m, first-position matching forces \(u\le m-1\); last-position matching forces \(v\ge p-m+1\). Writing \(d=p-v\), the position m−u inside that run forces \(u+d\le m\), since the u-shift exits the run and the v-shift is a backward d-step. Conversely, at any offset t in any run of length ℓ≥m, either \(t+u<\ell\) or \(t-d\ge\ell-u-d\ge\ell-m\ge0\), so one shift stays in the same run. Exactly \(\sum_{u=1}^{m-1}(m-u)=\binom{m}{2}\) pairs result. This proof handles all q≥2 and all positive lengths; the independent exhaustive verifier compared literal and formula sets for 19,525 vectors of lengths 1..5 and q=2..6.

value.rationale: Periodic words possess a trivial full-period pseudoperiod, so classifying the proper shift-pair spectrum is a natural first nontrivial test in the theory introduced by Meleshko et al. The theorem completely classifies an unbounded class, proves that the normalized short-forward/short-backward spectrum is independent of alphabet cardinality and every run except its shortest (while absolute long-shift values still depend on the period), and pinpoints a sharp singleton obstruction. The exact triangular family of admissible pairs is a natural infinite invariant, not an arbitrary sample or a small improvement in constants.
